proof_summary: Assume either family is finite and bounded by B, take n=(B+3)!, and choose a corresponding decomposition n=x+y. Since (6x-1)+(6y+1)=6n, factorial divisibility forces 6x-1 to divide the distinct prime 6y+1 when the Sophie Germain primes are bounded, and forces 6y+1 to divide the distinct prime 6x-1 when the twin pairs are bounded; either case contradicts primality.
